reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes participation in the Forsage system by claiming unusually high personal earnings, stating that viewers can also earn money, and directing them to call the displayed number. The dashboard shows a large team count, Forsage program matrices, and a personal link inviting viewers to sign up with the promoter's upline, indicating recruitment-linked earning claims rather than neutral commentary.

citations.quote: My Profit today is 345$ In R.P.W I got income of 50,000 on single day And you can also earn money in this system
Call me on the given number and I show you the difference

opening.argument: Judge, read the earnings language narrowly. The speaker says viewers “can” earn, not that they will earn a fixed amount. The figures are presented as the speaker’s own reported results, and the offer is to show viewers the difference if they call. That is a limited personal demonstration, not an express guarantee of returns. The claims may deserve scrutiny, but these words alone do not establish a promise that every viewer will profit.

citations.quote: My Profit today is 345$ In R.P.W I got income of 50,000 on single day And you can also earn money in this system
Call me on the given number and I show you the difference

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited earnings statement distinguishes the speaker’s claimed income from what viewers “can” earn; it does not promise them the same result. A request to call may be promotional, but the quoted invitation is to be shown a difference. Even the displayed dashboard does not, by itself, verify how its figures were generated or establish a guaranteed payout to a new participant.

citations.quote: My Profit today is 345$ In R.P.W I got income of 50,000 on single day And you can also earn money in this system
Call me on the given number and I show you the difference

true_side_reply.rebuttal: “Can” is not a guarantee, but the speaker still uses claimed earnings to encourage viewers to earn in the system and call. The dashboard also displays a team count and Forsage program matrices. The defense’s narrow reading of the wording does not account for the recruitment context visible alongside the pitch.

citations.quote: My Profit today is 345$ In R.P.W I got income of 50,000 on single day And you can also earn money in this system Call me on the given number and I show you the difference

opening.argument: Judge, the visible subject is an account dashboard: the video shows a profile, figures, and program panels while the speaker describes personal results. “Check” and “I show you” frame the presentation as something viewers can inspect, rather than evidence that a transaction occurs in the video. A demonstration of an account can be promotional without proving that viewers are being promised the displayed results or told to pay to obtain them.

citations.quote: Okay Champions, you can check my Fat. My Profit today is 345$ In R.P.W I got income of 50,000 on single day
Call me on the given number and I show you the difference

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening treats the dashboard’s team and matrices as proof of the mechanism behind the earnings claim. Those visible panels identify what the speaker is showing, but they do not trace a payment to recruitment. The speaker’s invitation to call is consistent with explaining the displayed account, even though it also promotes contact.

citations.quote: Call me on the given number and I show you the difference

true_side_reply.rebuttal: This is more than an account walkthrough. The speaker tells viewers they can earn in the system and asks them to call. The displayed personal link explicitly invites a nonmember to sign up with this upline. Calling the dashboard a demonstration does not remove its role in a recruitment pitch built around earnings claims.

citations.quote: And you can also earn money in this system Call me on the given number and I show you the difference

opening.argument: Judge, the personal link and upline invitation can be read as a referral promotion. The supplied material shows an earning claim, a way to sign up, and a request to call, but it does not show a required deposit, a request for credentials, or an explanation that the speaker’s income comes from recruiting viewers. Those missing steps matter: a referral link and an unverified income claim are grounds for caution, not, on their own, proof of the claimed scam mechanism.

citations.quote: My Profit today is 345$ In R.P.W I got income of 50,000 on single day And you can also earn money in this system Call me on the given number and I show you the difference

rebuttal.rebuttal: The personal link does invite sign-up with an upline, and the dashboard shows team and matrix information. But the cited material does not explain how a new member’s sign-up affects the speaker’s earnings, or show a deposit instruction. The prosecution’s reading is plausible; the visible evidence does not establish every step of that reading.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A deposit screen or compensation formula is not necessary to understand the pitch shown here. The speaker pairs striking personal income claims with “you can also earn,” directs viewers to call, and displays a sign-up invitation tied to an upline beside Forsage program matrices. The defense identifies details that are not shown, but does not explain away the recruitment-linked promotion that is shown.
